title: Outreach sequence drafts — Customer Reference Program (AEs/CSMs)
content:
Doc purpose
- Provide email + LinkedIn outreach copy variants for AEs/CSMs to recruit 3–5 design partners for Redwood’s Customer Reference Program.
- Two tracks: (A) Reference calls only (private) and (B) Public case study (logo/quotes + optional metrics/ranges).
- Keep tone: developer-first, respectful of time, clear about approvals + what’s optional.

IMPORTANT GUARDRAILS (please read before sending)
- Do not send if account is marked “do-not-contact” for marketing/reference asks.
- Coordinate internally first: AE + CSM align on ask, timing, and “what’s in it for them.”
- Never promise publication, specific metrics, or specific language. All public content requires customer approval + Redwood Legal review.
- Offer a low-lift first step: 15–20 min intro, or “reference calls only” if they’re not ready for public.
- If they have compliance constraints: offer anonymized story, high-level statements, or metrics as ranges (or none).

Personalization tokens (use consistently)
- {{first_name}} / {{last_name}}
- {{title}}
- {{company}}
- {{use_case}} (e.g., “LLM search + support assistant”, “RAG summarization for claims docs”)
- {{deployment}} (Hosted API / Dedicated / Private)
- {{why_now}} (e.g., “you’re nearing production rollout”, “you hit steady-state traffic”, “security review completed”)
- {{champion_moment}} (e.g., “p95 latency improvements”, “SLA confidence”, “routing/fallback”, “cost controls via batching/caching”)
- {{relationship_owner}} (AE/CSM name)
- {{calendar_link}} (Calendly or equivalent)
- {{legal_review_window}} (default: 7–10 business days)
- {{incentive_option}} (see below)

Incentive options (choose ONE; keep optional)
- Conference sponsorship credit (pre-approved; amounts vary)
- Extended Redwood Optimize trial / additional Optimize features for X months
- Charitable donation in customer’s name (if policy allows)

Suggested subject lines (mix and match)
- “Quick ask: Redwood reference program (low lift)”
- “{{company}} + Redwood story (Dedicated/Private)?”
- “Would you be open to a 15-min reference chat?”
- “Case study idea: {{use_case}} (you control what’s shared)”
- “Private reference calls only? (no public logo needed)”

SEQUENCE A — Reference calls only (private; no logo required)

A1) Initial ask (email) — AE or CSM
Subject: Quick ask: Redwood reference program (low lift)
Hi {{first_name}},

Hope you’re doing well. I’m reaching out with a small ask related to {{company}}’s work on {{use_case}}.

We’re putting together a short list of customers who might be open to occasional reference calls with teams evaluating Redwood (typically late-stage Dedicated/Private deals). The format is simple: a 25–30 minute call, we prep you with context, and you can decline any question.

Given {{champion_moment}}, I think your perspective would be really helpful to peers.

Would you be open to:
1) A quick 15-minute intro to align on boundaries and topics you’re comfortable with, and then
2) Potentially 1 call per quarter (or whatever cadence works for you)?

If yes, you can grab a time here: {{calendar_link}}. If easier, reply with a couple times next week.

Thanks either way,
{{relationship_owner}}
{{title}}, Redwood Inference


A2) Follow-up (email) — 4–5 business days later
Subject: Re: quick ask (reference calls)
Hi {{first_name}} — bumping this in case it got buried.

Totally fine if now isn’t a good time. If you’re open to it, we can keep this very lightweight:
- focus on your experience with {{deployment}} (no sensitive details)
- we handle scheduling + prep
- you can set limits (e.g., max 1 call/month, cooldown period)

Want me to send a few proposed time slots, or would you prefer to revisit later in {{next_quarter_or_month}}?

Thanks,
{{relationship_owner}}


A3) “Soft yes / need more detail” response (email)
Subject: Re: reference calls — what we’d cover
Hi {{first_name}},

Great — here’s what we typically cover on a reference call (and what we avoid):

Typical topics (opt-in):
- Why you chose Redwood for {{use_case}}
- What improved for your team (latency/reliability/cost, optional)
- How you run {{deployment}} (high level)
- Operational experience (rollouts, fallback policies, observability)

We avoid:
- Anything confidential about your customers, proprietary prompts, internal metrics you don’t want to share, security posture details beyond what you approve
- Competitor “trash talk”

We’ll send you a 1-page brief 24–48 hours in advance, and you can always say “I’d rather not answer that.”

If that works, here’s my link: {{calendar_link}}.

Best,
{{relationship_owner}}


A4) Soft no handling (email)
Subject: Re: quick ask
Hi {{first_name}},

Thanks for the quick reply — completely understood.

Two lower-lift options, if either is feasible:
- Option 1: We keep you “on standby” for a single call in the next 6 months (we’ll ask first).
- Option 2: You share 2–3 bullets we can use internally (no attribution) about what mattered most in your evaluation.

If neither works, no worries — we’ll pause asks on this topic.

Appreciate you,
{{relationship_owner}}


SEQUENCE B — Public case study (logo + quotes; metrics optional)

B1) Initial ask (email) — AE or CSM
Subject: {{company}} + Redwood story? (you control what’s shared)
Hi {{first_name}},

{{why_now}} and it made me think: would {{company}} be open to partnering on a short customer story about {{use_case}} on Redwood {{deployment}}?

What this is:
- A 30–45 min interview (we do the writing)
- A draft you can edit (full approval before anything goes live)
- Optional: logo + 1–2 quotes + high-level results (exact metrics optional; we can use ranges or omit)

Why we’re asking:
- Your experience with {{champion_moment}} is exactly what prospects ask about (latency/cost/reliability + deployment flexibility).

If you’re open to it, we can start with a 15-minute scoping call to confirm what you’re comfortable sharing publicly and who needs to approve on your side.

Does next week work? Here’s my link: {{calendar_link}}.

Thanks,
{{relationship_owner}}


B2) Follow-up (email) — 4–5 business days later
Subject: Re: {{company}} story — draft + approval-first process
Hi {{first_name}},

Quick follow-up. We can make this as conservative as you need:
- We can write it without naming specific internal systems
- We can use general statements (e.g., “improved p95 latency” / “reduced spend”) without numbers
- If metrics are included, you control the level (exact numbers vs ranges)

We also work around your approval process. Standard review window is {{legal_review_window}}, but we can extend.

Open to a short intro call? {{calendar_link}}

Best,
{{relationship_owner}}


B3) Scheduling email (once they agree)
Subject: Case study interview — agenda + prep
Hi {{first_name}},

Thanks — looking forward to it. Here’s a proposed agenda for the interview (30–45 min):
1) Background: what {{company}} built ({{use_case}})
2) Constraints: what you needed (security, SLA, cost targets, time-to-value)
3) Implementation: what running on Redwood {{deployment}} looks like (high-level)
4) Outcomes: what changed (metrics optional; ranges OK)
5) Approvals: who needs to review (brand/legal/compliance) + preferred attribution

Prep (optional):
- Any before/after numbers you’re comfortable sharing (even privately)
- Architecture sketch (we can draft one for review)

Invite attached. If anyone else should join (e.g., security/compliance, platform lead), happy to include them.

Best,
{{relationship_owner}}


B4) “Can’t do logo / can’t be public” pivot (email)
Subject: Re: customer story options
Hi {{first_name}},

Understood — and thank you for considering it.

If public logo/quotes aren’t possible, we still have two options:
- Private reference calls only (no public mention)
- An anonymized story (e.g., “Enterprise healthcare provider”) with no logo; still requires your approval

If either is workable, I can share what that looks like and keep the lift minimal.

Thanks,
{{relationship_owner}}


B5) “We can’t share metrics” handling (email)
Subject: Re: metrics — totally optional
Hi {{first_name}},

No problem at all — metrics are optional.

We can structure the story around:
- decision criteria (what you needed and why)
- implementation approach (high-level)
- operational outcomes (e.g., “more predictable latency,” “simpler rollouts,” “improved reliability via fallback routing”) without numbers

If later you decide you’re comfortable with ranges (e.g., “~20–30% improvement”), we can add them, but we won’t push for it.

Would you still be open to the interview?

Best,
{{relationship_owner}}


LINKEDIN VARIANTS (short)

L1) First touch — reference calls only
Hi {{first_name}} — quick question. Would {{company}} be open to being a private Redwood reference (occasional 25–30 min calls with late-stage prospects)? Very low lift; you set boundaries + cadence. If yes, happy to share details.

L2) First touch — public case study
Hi {{first_name}} — we’re capturing a few customer stories about production LLM inference (Dedicated/Private). Your work on {{use_case}} stood out. Open to a short interview? You control what’s shared; full approval before anything is published.

L3) Follow-up
Just bumping this, {{first_name}} — totally fine if timing isn’t right. If public isn’t possible, we can also do private references only.


VOICEMAIL (optional, AE-led)
“Hi {{first_name}}, it’s {{relationship_owner}} from Redwood Inference. Quick ask: we’re looking for 2–3 customers open to occasional reference calls about running {{use_case}} on Redwood {{deployment}}. Very low lift and you control what you share. I’ll send an email with details—feel free to reply with a yes/no or just a better time to chat.”


NOTES FOR SENDING / INTERNAL CHECKLIST
- Confirm customer health + readiness with CSM before any ask.
- For enterprise/compliance-heavy accounts: propose starting with reference calls only.
- Always route any public logo/quote request through the consent process.
- Track outcome in HubSpot (Reference Program fields) and post a brief note in #marketing (or designated channel).

Open questions / TODOs (as of last edit)
- Finalize standard “cadence cap” language (proposal: max 2 calls/month + 30-day cooldown).
- Confirm which incentives are allowed by region/customer policy (esp. public sector).
- Add an AE-facing snippet about how to position this for procurement-sensitive accounts.
